articleTitle: Deep Learning-Driven Channel Estimation Technique for Intelligent Reflecting Surface-Assisted Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: To address the issue of low channel estimation accuracy in intelligent reflecting surface (IRS)-assisted communication systems, a channel estimation scheme based on a Channel Denoising Network (CDN) is proposed, modeling the channel estimation problem as a channel noise elimination problem. First, traditional algorithms are used to perform an initial estimation of the received pilot signals, and then the estimates are fed into the channel estimation network to learn noise information and perform denoising, thereby recovering accurate channel coefficients. To enhance the network's denoising capability, an attention mechanism module and a dilated convolution module are designed to improve the extraction of primary noise information, while a feature fusion module is designed to prevent the loss of shallow features. Simulation results show that, compared to the classic DNCNN and CDRN networks, the proposed method reduces the normalized mean square error (NMSE) by an average of 2 to 2.89 dB across different signal-to-noise ratios.

articleTitle: A Lightweight Intrusion Detection System for In-Vehicle Bus Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: Vehicle networks designed based on Service-Oriented Architecture (SOA) present considerable benefits while they are subject to substantial cybersecurity vulnerabilities. For the Controller Area Network (CAN) protocol with weak security protections, a lightweight Intrusion Detection System (IDS) based on Renyi entropy is proposed. The proposed scheme employs the real-vehicle dataset for offline training of the IDS, which is subsequently utilized for real-time online detection. By employing the more sensitive Renyi entropy in place of the traditional Shannon entropy, the detection accuracy has been significantly improved. Comparative studies with other methods, along with adaptability studies across three vehicle models demonstrate that the proposed scheme exhibits superior detection performance and adaptability. The average detection accuracy exceeds 98% across all scenarios.

articleTitle: A Secure Coding Scheme Based on Serially Concatenated Convolutional Code
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: With the increasing number of wireless devices, the demand for secure message transmission is growing. Ensuring reliable and secure transmission is a key goal in physical layer security. Traditional models use layered design with encryption and channel coding. Recent research focuses on secure error-correcting codes, which could be a candidate for post-quantum cryptography. The challenge lies in designing a code that combines encryption and error correction without compromising decoding performance, while balancing computational resources and reducing system delays. This paper proposes a simplified scheme that integrates encryption and coding based on serially concatenated convolutional codes. By using a two-dimensional chaotic map to control the permutation matrix, interleaver, and puncturing pattern, the coding generator achieves dynamic changes within the period. It also analyzes the security under chosen plaintext attacks and compares the decoding performance of this scheme with the original coding scheme. The proposed scheme achieves a balance between encryption and reliability without significant loss in decoding performance.

articleTitle: Dynamic Obstacle Detection for Quadrotors with Event Cameras
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: Quadrotors based on traditional RGB cameras cannot effectively detect moving targets when facing high-speed moving obstacles, resulting in obstacle avoidance failure. Event cameras provide hardware support for capturing high-speed moving objects. This paper proposes a dynamic target detection method from the perspective of drones based on polar time difference surfaces. This method uses the spatial dislocation phenomenon of different polarities triggered by moving objects in the event stream to obtain the polar time difference surface, and finally realizes fast detection of dynamic targets through four-neighborhood depth-first search clustering. Experimental results show that this method obtains dynamic objects in the event stream with a delay of 5.92 milliseconds, which is 48.7% (5.63 milliseconds) less time than the existing motion target detection method, and improves the average detection recall rate, precision rate, and accuracy rate, proving the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Research on the Application of Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface Technology in Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: Reconfigurabl e Intelligent Surface (RIS), as an emerging technology, has demonstrated significant potential for application in the field of radar. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of the basic principles, advantages, and research on the application of RIS in radar systems. Firstly, the fundamental principles of RIS are thoroughly analyzed, along with its notable advantages over traditional technologies. Subsequently, the application of RIS in various aspects of radar systems, including target detection, parameter estimation, radar jamming and anti-jamming, and radar-communication integration, is elaborated in detail, showcasing how RIS can significantly enhance the performance of radar systems. Finally, the future development trends of RIS in the radar field are discussed, including dynamic environmental adaptability, intelligent management, low-power and low-cost designs, as well as integrated designs, and future research directions are explored.

articleTitle: Traffic Offloading Based on Bidirectional Auction in LEO Satellite Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: The paper presents a traffic offloading algorithm based on a bidirectional auction mechanism designed to balance traffic distribution in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite networks. By utilizing Inter-Satellite Links (ISLs), the algorithm transfers data from overloaded satellites to those with available capacity, improving overall network throughput and reducing end-to-end hops and energy consumption. Satellites exchange bandwidth and load information through detection packets sent to a ground station, which acts as an auction center, matching overloaded and underloaded satellites. Simulations show that the proposed algorithm outperforms other baseline methods in terms of throughput and energy efficiency under different load conditions. The algorithm enhances feeder link utilization and alleviates network congestion effectively.

articleTitle: Research on Optimization of Edge Detection Algorithm Based on Binocular Camera
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: Edge detection is one of the core technologies in digital image processing and computer vision, and has been widely applied in fields such as image recognition and remote sensing image processing. This article proposes an optimization scheme for edge detection algorithm, which collects image information through binocular cameras and caches it in memory. After grayscale transformation preprocessing, the classic SOBEL algorithm and optimized SOBEL algorithm are used to extract edge information, obtain binary images, and display them on the LCD screen in real time. Through practical testing, the optimized algorithm can effectively solve the problem of detecting edges that are too coarse in the original algorithm, and improve the accuracy of detection and positioning. This system can be widely applied in fields such as medical imaging and autonomous driving.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Radar-Based Bathroom Fall Detection using Time-Frequency Features
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: Falls in the elderly are a major public health problem. In this paper, an effective fall detection method based on millimeter wave radar system is proposed. Using the time-frequency characteristics of radar echoes, the signal-to-noise ratio is significantly improved by least squares adaptive filtering to eliminate interference, and classification is performed by combining short-time Fourier transform (STFT) and machine learning algorithms KNN (Nearest Neighbor), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) and Decision Tree (DT). By collecting data from two idle bathrooms, data from four actions were collected and the effectiveness of the machine learning SVM, KNN and MLP algorithms were verified by the measured data, in which the classification performance of SVM was better than the other three algorithms.

articleTitle: SwinDCA-Net: Leveraging Swin Transformer and Dynamic Connection Attention for Medical Image Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: This paper introduces SwinDCA-Net, a novel architecture tailored for medical image segmentation, with a specific emphasis on vessel segmentation. The model incorporates Swin Transformer Modules into the U-Net framework, blending local feature extraction with global context modeling to enhance the segmentation of complex structures. Additionally, a Dynamic Connection Attention Module is implemented within the skip connections, allowing for adaptive reweighting of features across different scales, thereby improving feature fusion. Through extensive experiments, SwinDCA-Net consistently demonstrates superior performance, surpassing existing models in metrics such as F1-Score, sensitivity, and accuracy. These results confirm the model's ability to accurately segment thin and complex structures.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Method for Detecting Foreign Object Intrusions in Power Transmission Lines Using Drone Aerial Photography
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: The issue of bird nests on power transmission lines has garnered significant attention in power systems due to the potential risk of equipment failure and large-scale blackouts. This paper proposes a bird nest detection method based on an improved YOLOv8 model. The method integrates the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) and Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP) into the YOLOv8 model to enhance the model's ability to capture bird nest features and improve detection accuracy. CBAM enhances the model's sensitivity to target features by combining spatial and channel attention mechanisms, while ASPP improves the model's detection capabilities across different scales through multi-scale feature extraction. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the improved YOLOv8-based bird nest detection method excels in terms of accuracy, recall, and detection speed. The application of this method is expected to significantly improve the efficiency and reliability of bird nest detection during power line inspections, thereby ensuring the stable operation of power systems.

articleTitle: Multipath-Based Physical Layer Authentication for Dynamic Meta-Surface Antenna Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: Wireless communications are vulnerable to attacks and jamming due to their broadcast nature, and establishing an authentication mechanism is one effective way to enhance security against malicious access. A physical layer authentication (PLA) scheme utilizing the multipath information is proposed in this paper. The atomic norm minimization algorithm and peak spectrum search algorithm are utilized to estimate the multipath information. By comparing the similarity of the multipath information in consecutive time slots, a binary hypothesis test is developed to verify the transmitter. Simulation results indicate that the proposed scheme can achieve a higher authentication probability.

articleTitle: Product Vectors in Quantum Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: Matrix theory play a fundamental role in classical and quantum computing. Among this paper, we study the fundamental concepts of some matrices including unitary matrix and Hermitian matrix, which may convert some initial qubits into various kinds of qubits. We also explore the fundamental concept of eigenvalues. Furthermore, we input the concept of product vectors. Finally we use above-mentioned concepts examing the entanglement witness for verifying the entanglement in quantum computing and circuits.

articleTitle: Obstruction Detection Based on Light Field Image Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: Detection of foreign object intrusion on railway track is a critical research topic to railway information systems. Current imaging systems often suffer from a lack of spatial scene information due to the reliance on single visible-light sensors. A light-field imaging-based scheme for foreign object intrusion detection is proposed. By extracting saliency features from light field data, it leverages the capability of light field cameras to simultaneously capture both RGB image information and depth information. Firstly, traditional manifold sorting (MR) algorithm is employed to improve the accuracy of RGB image detection. Then the salient features of depth images are extracted as a supplement to RGB image processing. Finally, an effective data fusion method is proposed to further highlight the object contour and suppress the background, so as to improve the detection performance. The experimental results show that the proposed light-field-based scheme has the application ability to detect foreign objects in rail transit environment efficiently.

articleTitle: Link Aggregation Based De-Stacking Design and Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: With the rapid development of big data such as in-vehicle and airborne, edge devices face the challenge of processing and transmitting large amounts of data. While providing high bandwidth and high reliability, traditional switch stacking and MLAG technologies have problems such as high port resource overhead and no support for cross-vendor device heterogeneity, which are not applicable to edge devices with limited resources. In this paper, we propose a de-stacking scheme for edge devices, which reduces Peer-Link interactions between switches and lowers port overhead by replicating ARP messages on the NIC side so that ARP messages are sent from all ports within the aggregation group, and at the same time improves the stability of system operation. The experiment verifies the performance of ARP double-sending on the simulation platform by modifying the Linux kernel. The experimental results show that the scheme can successfully realize ARP double-issuing and improve the reliability and transmission capacity of the network.

articleTitle: An Efficient Multi-Party Private Set Intersection Protocol
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: Privacy Set Intersection (PSI) is an important Secure Multi-Party Computation (SMC) technique that allows participants to securely compute the intersection of their data sets without revealing any other information. To address the unfairness issues present in existing protocols, this paper proposes a fair multi-party PSI protocol based on Three-Hash Garbled Cuckoo Table (3H-GCT) and secret sharing. The protocol uses 3H-GCT as a data structure to store the data of each participant and employs secret sharing and share permutation techniques to protect data privacy, preventing the leakage of individual elements during the interaction. The core of the protocol lies in the cloud server performing bitwise XOR operations on the 3H-GCTs of each participant to compute the intersection, and then sending the intersecting 3H-GCT to all participants, ensuring the fairness of the protocol. Correctness analysis and security proofs show that the protocol is secure in a semi-honest environment. Experimental data indicates that the protocol has lower communication costs and computation time compared to existing protocols.

articleTitle: Traffic-Load-Aware Multipath Routing in LEO Satellite Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: In this paper, we present a traffic-load-aware multipath routing algorithm in LEO satellite networks. The MDL algorithm has three main components: network state collection, link cost definition, and multipath routing. Network state collection builds a shared information repository and topology. Link cost calculations guide path selection. The multipath routing mechanism identifies the optimal path and an alternative one. If the optimal path faces node failure or congestion, traffic can be rerouted through the alternative path, reducing network congestion effectively. Simulation results show that it can decrease latency and increase throughput compared to baseline algorithms.

articleTitle: Simulation Study on the Influence Parameters of Radon Detection in the Air
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: Radon in the environment poses a significant health risk to the human respiratory system. Accurate measurement of radon concentration not only helps identify potential sources of radon pollution but also provides a basis for implementing appropriate protective measures, thereby effectively reducing the harm of radon gas to human health. Therefore, conducting monitoring and assessment of radon concentration is a crucial aspect of ensuring public health. Pulse ionization chamber can be used to measure radon levels in the air, but it faces challenges such as long charge collection times and sensitivity to environmental changes. This paper adopted Garfield++ to construct a simulation model of the ionization chamber, aiming to research the influence of various parameters on charge collection time in depth. The influence of the size parameters of both cylindrical and flat-plate ionization chambers on the maximum charge collection time is researched. Additionally, the effects of different gas parameters of air as the working gas on the charge transport process are considered, and the influence of maximum charge collection time on signal output circuit design is analyzed. The results of the research provide important references for the optimization of detector design.

articleTitle: Designing Customizable Privacy-Preserving Localization in Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: Localization technology plays an important role in many Internet of Things (IoT) applications. The requirements of privacy preservation levels may vary depending on the application scenario. However, most of the existing privacy-preserving localization schemes adopt a fixed privacy preservation level, which can not meet the requirements of customizable privacy-preserving localization. In order to solve the issue, this paper designs a customizable privacy-preserving localization algorithm (CPPL). Firstly, by setting three levels of privacy preservation, anchor node users can choose to customize their privacy protection level based on their own privacy protection requirements. The privacy level noise they need is calculated, and the noise-added location information is sent to the target node. Secondly, to preserve the private noise level, the anchor node sends the privacy level noise plus zero-sum noise to the target node. The target node calculates and infers its own location by using the location information with added privacy level noise sent by the anchor node and the privacy level noise information after adding zero-sum noise. The experimental results show that the designed algorithm ensures privacy protection and localization accuracy while meeting the user's customizable requirements.

articleTitle: Energy Harvesting Node Assisted Secure Communication System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: In this paper, we study the problem of secure communication between a source S and a target D in the face of an eavesdropping node with the help of multiple energy harvesting (EH) nodes. The energy harvesting relay transmission (EHRT) and energy harvesting jammer transmission (EHJT) schemes are proposed, and their outage and interception probabilities are derived. Simulation results show that the EJT scheme outperforms the ERT scheme in overall performance.

articleTitle: Covert Communication via InfoGAN-Based Image Generation-Steganography
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: A covert communication technique based on image generation by InfoGAN, which harnesses InfoGAN's capability of reconstructing information, is investigated. In the proposed InfoGAN framework, secrecy data is embedded into randomly generated images through the generator model at the transmitter and a classifier model deployed at the receiver can decode the embedded information bits. It achieves covert transmission of the secrecy data while maintaining a high level of security and stealth. By leveraging the adversarial nature of InfoGAN, the method ensures that the hidden information is embedded into the images without compromising the visual quality, making it difficult for observers to notice the presence of the embedded data. Through experimental results, it is demonstrated that the proposed method not only successfully hides and restores the secrecy information, but also offers clear advantages in security and stealth. The generated images containing secrecy data are visually indistinguishable from images in the data set, ensuring that the hidden information is hard to detect. Furthermore, the method introduces an additional robust security layer through the adversarial learning framework of InfoGan, making it highly resilient to potential attacks.

articleTitle: Research on Environmental 3D Object Detection Technology Fusing LIDAR Dot-Cloud and Vision Image
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: With the rapid development of autonomous driving and industrial automation, 3D object detection plays a crucial role in understanding and interpreting the surrounding environment. Single sensors, such as LiDAR or cameras, often face issues of data missing and insufficient information in complex scenarios. To address these limitations, This study designed a 3D object detection method that fusingLIDAR dot-cloud and Vision Image. Firstly, a joint calibration of LiDAR and camera is conducted to unify the coordinate systems, followed by Beidou timing to achieve synchronization of fusion signal time reference. Next, images captured by the camera are input into an improved YOLOv8 algorithm for 2D object detection, generating 2D bounding boxes for the objects. These 2D predictions are then used, along with the joint calibration parameters, to deduce the 3D conical regions of the objects. Finally, the DBSCAN clustering algorithm is employed to obtain accurate 3D information of the objects. The feasibility of this method is demonstrated through hardware platform construction and testing.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Efficacy of Pre-Trained ImageNet Weights for Constellation Diagram Classification Using Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: Constellation diagram classification is crucial for selecting the appropriate demodulation method in communication systems, as it allows for accurate interpretation of modulated signals. In this context, it is essential to investigate the impact of using pretrained ImageNet weights in classical CNN models for this task. This paper explores the effect of ImageNet pretrained weights on the classification of simulated constellation diagrams, including QAM-16, QAM-32, and QAM-64 modulation schemes. Three deep learning models, VGG, ResNet, and MobileNet, were evaluated using accuracy as the primary performance metric. The models were trained both with and without ImageNet pretrained weights to compare their effectiveness. The experimental results demonstrated that incorporating ImageNet weights led to significant performance improvements in most models. MobileNet, in particular, achieved the highest accuracy, showcasing its ability to effectively learn from pretrained weights and generalize well to the constellation classification task. ResNet showed moderate improvements, while VGG failed to benefit from the pretrained weights. These findings suggest that smaller, more efficient models like MobileNet are better suited for tasks with limited data. In conclusion, this study validates the effectiveness of deep learning models for constellation diagram classification and highlights the benefits of using ImageNet pretrained weights to enhance performance, especially for models with fewer parameters. Future work could focus on exploring more complex modulation schemes and expanding the range of models tested.

articleTitle: Channel Estimation for UAV-Enabled mmWave Massive MIMO Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: The Doppler frequency shift caused by the high mobility of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) can seriously degrade the performance of communication systems. In this paper, we propose an angle of arrival (AOA) estimation method with Doppler shift compensation for the UAV-enabled millimeter-wave (mmWave) system which is equipped with a large-scale uniform linear array (ULA) and used to serve multiple users simultaneously. Specifically, we apply discrete Fourier transform (DFT) and phase rotation methods to estimate the Doppler shift. Besides, combined with the orthogonal pilot matrix, we can derive the channel state information (CSI), Doppler shift, and AOA of each user well. Finally, simulation results are provided to corroborate our proposed studies.

articleTitle: Primary School Students' ICT Competences: A Hierarchical and Multidimensional Machine Learning Assessment Model
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: This study established a multidimensional and multilevel information literacy evaluation model using the multi-label multiclassification method in machine learning. Our presented model includes five dimensions: information, communication, content creation, security, and problem-solving. Each dimension was divided into three levels: basic (A), intermediate (B), and advanced (C). The model was then used to evaluate the information literacy of 3,233 primary school students. The results showed that most students were at the lower A level in the dimensions of information, communication, content creation, and problem-solving, while in the security dimension, most students were at the intermediate B level. This study provides a deep understanding of primary school students' information literacy from multiple perspectives and levels and can serve as a basis for education managers to understand the status of primary school students' information literacy and develop targeted information literacy education strategies.

articleTitle: A Gait Control Method for Bipedal Robots Based on Reward Function Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: The intelligent control of walking of humanoid robots is one of the key research directions in the field of robotics research, but the traditional motion model's constraint on the center of mass makes it difficult for robots to maintain walking stability and simulate human gait at the same time for its excessive attention on stability. Compared with the traditional deep reinforcement learning algorithm, the DDPG algorithm has the ability to handle continuous action space and high-dimensional state space, and has a wide application prospect in many practical problems. We proposed a bipedal robot control method based on reward function optimization to enable the robot to achieve both stable high-speed movement and human gait imitation. This paper combines the physical characteristics of the bipedal robot to establish a control system based on the DDPG algorithm. At the same time, the reward function is designed to guide the robot to learn the correct walking strategy. Through the comparative test, the weight limit ratio of each reward function for the bipedal robot to stably increase the speed is given. The simulation results show that the method proposed in this paper has good practicality and effectiveness.

articleTitle: Multi-Level Backup Link Architecture for SRv6 Network Fault Recovery
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: In recent years, segment routing IPv6(SRv6) technology is usually used in cross-domain network communication fields to achieve end-to-end communication, but network links often fail. The traditional method of recovery in the forwarding layer includes directly sending a new link or switching to the backup link that is reserved in advance. However, the time limit for failure recovery of the above method is relatively slow. In order to make the faulty SRv6 network recovery quickly, this article designs a multilevel protection backup link architecture. According to the characteristics of SRv6 network head node that can plan path flexibly and SRv6 application scenarios are diversified, the pre-issued backup path rules are stored and effective according to the architecture relationship. This architecture can simplify the processing flow of forwarding layer for backup links during failure recovery, and steadily reduce the failure recovery time of forwarding layer. The experimental results show that the use of this architecture in the forwarding layer can reduce the duration of the forwarding layer by approximately 90%. Moreover, the packet loss rate, delay and bandwidth of the link after the failure recovery are consistent with those before the failure, and the fault recovery effect is also very good.

articleTitle: A Transformer Based Cycle Posture Detection System Using 3D Pose Estimation Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: The concept of “form recognition” has had a lot of applications from different times, such as art, training sports, and movement analysis. Nonetheless, bicycle configuration recognition is one of the areas that led to the development of a model that only earlier didn't receive much attention up to recently. The posture of cycling is also crucial for human health, in order to better analyze and correct posture, in our study, we present a bike form detection model which is a product designed for the use of leisure cyclists. Cyclists will be able to utilize this model to inspect whether they have a good sitting position, affect their acceleration, and improve their own well-being. We can now evaluate the position of joints and develop a system of grades with just a phone camera being used yet still achieving top level accuracy. In addition, our 3D pose estimation has been brought to cycling through our unique database that has shown remarkable results in terms of rider's posture improvement.

articleTitle: Joint Three-Task Optical Performance Monitoring with High Performance and Generalizability Using a Meta-Learning Algorithm in WDM Transmissions
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: We propose a meta-learning CNN-attention algorithm for joint three-task optical performance monitoring using IQ signal feature histogram data, demonstrating high performance in single-channel transmissions and excellent generalizability in five-channel WDM transmissions, outperforming the traditional transfer learning algorithm.

articleTitle: Research on Few-Shot Object Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: Object recognition is a crucial task in the realm of computer vision, aimed at identifying and pinpointing a particular object within an image. In practical scenarios, a lack of sufficient training samples frequently hinders the training of deep learning models, presenting a significant challenge. FSOR was created to address this issue. In this paper, the basic concepts, main methods, challenges and latest research progress of few-shot object recognition are reviewed, and its potential in practical application is discussed.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Multi Keyword Searchable Encryption Scheme Based on Counting Bloom Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of high computation and storage cost of keyword ciphertexts in existing encryption schemes, this paper proposes a fuzzy multi-keyword searchable encryption scheme based on counting Bloom filter. The efficient dynamic management of keywords and fuzzy matching function are realized by introducing the count Bloom filter and local sensitive hashing technique. This scheme not only improves the ciphertext retrieval efficiency, but also ensures the security under adaptive keyword selection attack. Experimental results show that this scheme exhibits good performance in both trapdoor generation time and keyword retrieval matching time.

articleTitle: Improved U-Net with Gray Channel Attention for Image Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: Image segmentation base on deep learning methods is an important direction in computer vision field. However, these models over-rely on color features in image segmentation tasks, which leads to poor segmentation effect in scenes with the interference of similar background colors. To solve this problem, this paper successfully improves the U-Net model by introducing the technical means of combining gray channel and attention mechanism. The experimental results show that compared with the original U-Net model, the average accuracy of the improved U-Net with gray channel attention has increased from 81.69% to 82.61%. At the same time, we apply this method mechanism to improved models of U-Net such as Attention U-Net and R2U-net, and similar effect is verified. These results verify that the combination of gray channel and attention mechanism can effectively improve the robustness and accuracy of deep learning model when processing color-similar background in image segmentation tasks. This work has important practical application value and provides a new solution for image segmentation tasks in complex scenes.

articleTitle: Multiscale Feature Extraction-Based Remote Sensing Image Matching Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: This paper addresses the challenges of feature extraction and real-time matching in heterogeneous remote sensing images caused by the differing imaging principles of various sensors. We propose a remote sensing image matching network based on Multiscale feature extraction. The network establishes a matching framework for aerial and satellite images, employing a Multiscale Feature Enhancement Module (MSFEM) to extract scale-invariant features and perform salient feature point detection. This approach effectively captures local features and contextual information from heterogeneous images. Subsequently, the feature points and descriptors are decoded and fed into the SuperGlue feature matching network for alignment. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed matching method improves matching accuracy by 13.79% compared to D2Net and by 2.86% compared to LoFTR, validating the network's potential for feature extraction and matching tasks in heterogeneous remote sensing imagery.

articleTitle: Research on Heterogeneous Network Data Fusion Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: The advent of the era of big data has led to the emergence of heterogeneous network data fusion as a prominent area of research. Heterogeneous network data is characterised by multimodality, multi-source, and high dimensionality, which presents significant challenges for traditional data fusion methods. These methods often encounter difficulties in processing such data, including issues such as information redundancy, data inconsistency, and high computational complexity. This paper proposes a heterogeneous network data fusion model based on a deep neural network. The model employs the Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) as its fundamental framework, utilising the deep neural network to facilitate joint feature representation learning on data from disparate modalities. The Adaptive Feature Reconstruction Module enables the model to learn the interrelationships between different modalities and to balance the importance of different modal features in the fusion process in a dynamic manner. Furthermore, we introduce an innovative cross-modal attention mechanism, which is capable of effectively capturing the coupling relationship between deep features in heterogeneous data, thereby enhancing the expressiveness and data fusion efficacy of the model. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model markedly enhances the accuracy of classification and regression tasks in comparison to traditional methodologies.

articleTitle: Enhanced 3D Style Transfer of Neural Radiance Fields via Generalized Gaussian Distribution Transformation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: The endeavor of 3D style transfer is to create styled novel perspectives of a 3D environment, ensuring consistency among multiple views. However, the majority of current works encounter problems such as color distortion or the loss of details in the styled outcomes, which are caused by the disregard for the holistic statistics of the reference image color style. To address these issues, we propose a method called ggdT-StyleRF based on the optimal transport theory of Generalized Gaussian Distribution (GGD). By integrating a GGD transformation step into the StyleRF workflow, we effectively combine color processing with 3D scene style transfer. The GGD transformation method was selected for its demonstrated flexibility and adaptability in statistical modeling, as well as its successful application in 2D image style transfer. Experimental results demonstrate that ggdT-StyleRF significantly enhances the transmission of the reference image color style while preserving the source image's texture structure. Notably, ggdT-StyleRF achieves substantial improvements in Frechet inception distance and Bhattacharyya distance, indicating a significant improvement in color style transfer without compromising geometric fidelity.

articleTitle: An Implantable Broadband Antenna for ISM-Band Applications with a Small, Multi-Slot Design
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: The human body is a complex dielectric environment, with each tissue layer possessing distinct dielectric constants, which can significantly impact the performance of antennas. To address the issue of unstable communication in implantable devices, a miniaturized, broadband, implantable antenna designed for the Industrial, Scientific, and Medical (ISM) band (2.4-2.48 GHz) is presented. The antenna has a compact volume of merely 6×6×0.53 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, achieved by introducing a zigzag slot, symmetrical rectangular slots, and multiple identically sized rectangular slots on the metallic patch, thereby realizing miniaturization. The antenna utilizes alumina ceramic as the dielectric substrate, covered with silicone on the top layer, endowing the antenna with biocompatibility. A rectangular ground plane is etched beneath the substrate to extend the antenna's impedance bandwidth. To simulate the antenna's in vivo working environment, simulations were conducted within a simulated human muscle tissue model. Test results indicate that the antenna's operational bandwidth reaches 15% (2.23-2.57 GHz), fully covering the ISM band.

articleTitle: A Simplified 256-APSK Soft Demapping Method and Implementation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: High-order amplitude phase shift keying (APSK) presents significant challenges in both hardware and software implementations for demapping due to its characteristics such as a large number of constellation points, high computational complexity, and pronounced nonlinear property. In this paper, a low complexity soft demapping method is proposed, where APSK modulation is equivalently decomposed into independent PSK and ASK modulations, and then the computational process of the Max-Log-Map algorithm is simplified in accordance with their respective distributions, resulting in an efficient yet low complexi-ty demapping algorithm. Simulation results indicate that for 256-APSK, the proposed method achieves identical performance to traditional demapping algorithms, with significantly reduced computational complexity.

articleTitle: An Empirical Path Loss Model for Low-Altitude Communication in Urban Scenario
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: Low-altitude communication is the key application scenario of future fifth-generation-advance (5G-A) and six-generation (6G) wireless communication. To achieve stable and reliable capability, it is important to establish a path loss model for low-altitude communication. The existing models are not applicable considering frequency band, distance range, and altitude range. This paper provides a modified path loss model based on measurement data. The validation results demonstrate that the proposed path loss model may achieve an acceptable degree of accuracy for both line-of-sight (LoS) and nonline-of-sight (NLoS) case in urban scenario. The proposed path loss model can help support the design of low-altitude communication networks in future.

articleTitle: Key Technical Points Analysis of the Civil Aviation Data Governance System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: As a new type of production factor, data is a crucial foundation for the digital transformation of the civil aviation industry. In the past two years, the Civil Aviation Administration of China (CAAC) has successively issued the “7+1” series of Smart Civil Aviation Data Governance Standards, providing guidance for industry data governance and offering solutions for “how to manage and use data” in civil aviation. This article combines national development trends and the current state of industry data to analyze the civil aviation data governance system and its construction key points through the interpretation of these series of standards.

articleTitle: Research on Physical Layer Key Generation and Agreement Technology Based on Wireless Channels
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: With the rapid development of wireless networks, the application of wireless devices in the field of communication is be-coming increasingly widespread. However, the openness of wire-less channels makes them susceptible to various factors such as channel interference, leading to increased network security risks. This paper investigates a physical layer key generation scheme based on wireless channels and designs a complete system for key generation in one-to-many scenarios. The system includes four stages of the key generation scheme: channel measurement, quan-tization, key agreement, and privacy amplification. In the channel measurement stage, a sequence-based method is used to ensure signal reciprocity. Additionally, in the privacy amplification stage, a rule for key selection and combination is designed to make the key practically applicable. Finally, the performance and security of the system are experimentally tested and analyzed.

articleTitle: Foreign Object Detection of Belt Conveyor Based on Enhanced YOLOv8 Model
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: Object detection on conveyor belts through computer vision currently faces several challenges. To address issues such as low performance and the scarcity of training and testing data, this paper proposes an improved solution based on YOLOv8. This paper incorporates various attention mechanisms, modifies, network structure of YOLOv8, and optimizes association matching using the EIOU algorithm. As a result, it can accurately detect foreign objects on the conveyor belt, including their categories and appearance features. Furthermore, this paper constructs a dataset by onsite collection and annotation. After labeling and categorizing the data, the dataset is used for training. Experimental results indicate that the improved algorithm enhances performance metrics such as accuracy, mAP50, and mAP50-95 compared to the baseline algorithm, YOLOv8n, and these results are validated on the test dataset.

articleTitle: Research on the Application of Integrated Communication Technology in Airports
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: Efficient and smooth communication command and dispatch is an important prerequisite for effectively handling various emergencies at airports in a short period of time. A typical flight support process in a large hub airport typically involves over 10 departments, 20 milestones, and over 100 task assignments and uploads. This type of support process may reach thousands of times per day, with over 10000 cross departmental, cross system, and cross terminal communications. A single telephone dispatch or manual switching of communication terminals can no longer fully meet the huge communication needs. The integrated communication technology can integrate and apply various communication modes with different transmission links, protocol standards and usage modes, and combine audio, video and positioning elements to achieve direct and seamless communication between different terminals. Therefore, building an interconnected integrated communication platform and applying it to the operation and command of large airports will effectively improve the efficiency and quality of various tasks.

articleTitle: Research on Filtering Algorithm of Bridge Vibration Signal Based on Millimeter Wave Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: Bridges play a crucial role in transportation networks, but accidents due to bridge health issues pose serious threats to safety. Millimeter-wave radar, a non-contact detection technology, is increasingly used for monitoring bridge health. This paper proposes a PSO-VMD-SWT algorithm to optimize VMD parameters using PSO, filter radar echo signals with SWT, and analyze bridge vibration signals through phase detection. Experimental validation using millimeter-wave radar and accelerometers confirmed the algorithm's effectiveness in detecting bridge health.

articleTitle: Design Simulation and Verification of a Key Negotiation Scheme Based on Physical Layer Noise Error Parameters in Optical Fibre Transmission Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: In this paper, a key negotiation method based on the local noise system error parameters is proposed, where the negotiating parties use the addition of Gaussian white noise at the receiving end to encrypt the received signals, thus ensuring the randomness of the negotiated key. The negotiation method is verified through simulation and its performance is analysed. Under the condition that the mean of the noise standard deviation distribution is 0.28, the quantification coefficient is 0.3, and the segment length is 1000, its negotiation efficiency can reach more than 80%, and the agreement rate of the two parties' keys can reach more than 98%.

articleTitle: Task-Parallel Resource Allocation for Power Network Query Engine Based on Cross-Platform Communication Protocols
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: The current parallel resource allocation model of power network query engine task is mostly based on informatization model processing, and the allocation efficiency of parallel resources is relatively low, resulting in the decreasing allocation frequency, for this reason, we propose to design and analyze the design and analysis of the parallel resource allocation method of power network query engine task based on the cross-platform communication protocol. According to the current determination, real-time resource collection and preprocessing are carried out first, matching of resource feature points is carried out, cross-platform communication protocols are adopted to improve the allocation efficiency of parallel resources, cross-platform communication protocols are constructed for parallel resource allocation model of electric power network query engine task, and adaptive adjustment is adopted to realize resource allocation processing. Test results show that: compared with the cloud edge dynamic measurement resource allocation method, intelligent cooperative user scheduling and resource allocation, this design of cross-platform communication protocol power network query engine task parallel resource allocation method ultimately results in a relatively high frequency of allocation, which indicates that this design of cross-platform communication protocol power network query engine task parallel resource allocation method of real-time processing efficiency machine is targeted to a high degree, the effect of allocation is significantly improved, which has practical application value and innovative significance.

articleTitle: A Method for Estimating the Total Retrieved Ground Ozone Based on Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: In view of the problems of time-consuming and poor accuracy in the estimation of the total amount of ground ozone inversion by the traditional estimation method, a ground ozone inversion total amount estimation method based on depth neural network is proposed. The total amount of surface ozone inversion is preliminarily estimated. First, satellite observations are simulated to determine the amount of radiation transfer. Through the forward modeling and inversion process, the simulation results are compared with the satellite observation results to obtain the total ozone preliminary valuation. Based on the deep neural network model, a training model for estimating the total amount of ground ozone inversion is constructed, and the training effect of the network model is improved by adaptively changing the learning efficiency, and then the correct total amount of ozone is obtained through the iterative process. The experimental results show that the estimated time of this method is 4.5 s when the total amount of ozone recovered on the ground is 120 m3/hr. In five experiments, the average estimation accuracy of the total surface ozone retrieved by this method is 94.5%. It is proved that the estimation method of total surface ozone based on depth neural network inversion is effective.

articleTitle: Homologous Image Registration Algorithm Based on Generalized Dual-Bootstrap Iterative Closest Point Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: Heterogeneous image registration is a critical field in computer vision, with broad applications in scene registration, image retrieval, and autonomous driving. Due to differences in sensor types and imaging conditions, heterogeneous images often exhibit significant appearance discrepancies, leading to errors when using traditional registration methods. To address this challenge, we propose the Enhanced Generalized Dual-Bootstrap Iterative Closest Point (E-GDB-ICP) algorithm, designed to improve the accuracy and robustness of heterogeneous image registration. The proposed algorithm first utilizes SIFT descriptors and a multi-scale keypoint detector to initialize feature points, significantly increasing initial registration accuracy. The feature point selection process is then refined to further enhance the reliability of matches. Additionally, a new image registration quality evaluation function is introduced, enabling the assessment of registration outcomes without requiring ground truth data. This makes it a valuable tool for real-world applications. Experimental validation on remote sensing and architectural image datasets demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed method, which achieves improved accuracy and robustness in heterogeneous image registration tasks.

articleTitle: Risk Analysis of Enterprise Cross-Network Data via DAE-BiLSTM and Fuzzy Bayesian Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: With the increasing severity of enterprise information security issues, the identification and evaluation of cross-network data risk has become one of the essential technologies to safeguard enterprise data and network security. However, traditional rule-based or signature-based anomaly detection methods are increasingly unable to cope with the complex and evolving forms of attacks, necessitating more intelligent and flexible detection mechanisms to counter these constantly changing threats. To address this, a method integrating denoising autoencoder (DAE) and bidirectional long short-term memory network (BiLSTM) is first proposed for monitoring the enterprise cross-network data traffic and identify the occurring abnormal risks. On this basis, we use a fuzzy Bayesian network to effectively measure these known abnormal risks. In the end, experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms traditional machine learning algorithms and other deep learning models across various evaluation metrics, exhibiting high accuracy and efficiency.

articleTitle: LCAF: A Novel Side-Channel Analysis Method Based on Self-Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
abstract: Cryptography technology is widely used in various fields to protect information security, and the security evaluation of cryptographic modules or chips themselves is also receiving increasing attention. Side-channel analysis is a method to extract sensitive information, such as secret keys, by analyzing side-information leaked during the operation of encryption devices. It largely avoids the complexity of traditional cryptanalysis, and greatly improves the efficiency of analysis attacks. In recent years, researchers have applied deep learning to side-channel analysis attacks, greatly improving the performance of analysis attacks. However, most deep learning methods still suffer from fast overfitting, slow convergence, and shallow feature extraction, and are only effective for specific scenarios. We propose a novel method LCAF based on Long-short term Memory (LSTM), Convolutional neural network (CNN), and self-attention mechanism. Experimental results on four different datasets show that our method outperforms the existing techniques, and can successfully recover the key with only few traces.
